Dining at Gateway Lodge is straightforward and well done rather than elaborate. Lakeside has a restaurant and lounge on site; Tamale serves guests on the property. The emphasis is on food that suits how people actually travel, an early breakfast before a meeting, something warm after a long drive north, an unhurried meal by the pool.

Gateway Lodge does not run a restaurant, and that is the point. A guest staying a week does not want a menu every evening; they want a fridge, a cooker and a table. Every unit has all three, which is what makes a long stay feel like living somewhere rather than visiting.

Tell us in advance and we will do our best to accommodate dietary requirements, early breakfasts before flights, and meals for groups travelling together. The most reliable way to arrange this is to mention it when you book, or to contact the property directly.

If your stay needs something the kitchen does not already have, tell us when you book and we will do our best to have it there. Groups travelling together can ask about units side by side, so one kitchen can cook for everybody.

A dining experience at Gateway Lodge is not a tasting menu and a wine pairing. It is a good meal, served properly, somewhere comfortable, by the pool at Lakeside, or at the end of a long day on the road in Tamale. That is what our guests actually ask for.

We do not run a restaurant. What we give you instead is a kitchen of your own and a neighbourhood worth walking into. Some nights that means cooking what you actually feel like; other nights it means somebody else cooking it two streets away.
Group meals, dietary requirements and early breakfasts are all straightforward when we know beforehand. Mention it when you book, or contact the property directly and we will arrange it.
If you want the fridge stocked before you land, or you are travelling as a group and want units near each other, mention it when you book and we will sort it out.
